Financial Information&#8221; of this Registration Statement.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">v</font></div></div></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_1895"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Item 1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Business</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Overview</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">West Coast Community Bancorp is a bank holding company headquartered in Santa Cruz, California that operates through its sole and wholly owned subsidiary, West Coast Community Bank, a California state-chartered bank.  Substantially all of our business activities are conducted through the Bank. The Bank operates 10 branches across the California Central Coast, which we define as the counties of Santa Cruz, Monterey, Santa Clara and San Luis Obispo, and primarily serves small- to medium-sized businesses, which we generally define as businesses with annual revenues of $100 million or less, service professionals and individuals. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Bank began business operations in February 2004 under the name Santa Cruz County Bank, and the Bank&#8217;s name was changed to West Coast Community Bank on April 1, 2025, following the closing of the Company&#8217;s acquisition of 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp on October 1, 2024. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Bank is supervised and regulated by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the &#8220;FDIC&#8221;) and the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation (the &#8220;DFPI&#8221;). Bancorp was incorporated in the State of California on November 10, 2009, and the Company obtained approval from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System on June 2, 2023 for Bancorp to become a bank holding company and became the sole shareholder of the Bank on August 18, 2023 following a reorganization transaction. This transaction was treated as an internal reorganization as all shareholders of the Bank became shareholders of Bancorp. As a bank holding company, Bancorp is subject to regulation and supervision by the Federal Reserve, including the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the &#8220;BHCA&#8221;).  </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our Common Stock is currently quoted over the counter on the OTC Markets Group LLC&#8217;s OTCQX under the symbol &#8220;WCCB.&#8221; The Company has applied to list its Common Stock with the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (&#8220;Nasdaq&#8221;) under the symbol &#8220;WCCB&#8221; concurrently with the effectiveness of this Registration Statement.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Some of the products and services that we offer include checking, savings and money market accounts, certificates of deposit, treasury and cash management services, commercial and industrial loans, commercial real estate loans, commercial construction and development loans, online banking and mobile banking. As of June 30, 2026, the Company had total consolidated assets of $2.9 billion, total loans held for investment of $2.3 billion, total deposits of  $2.5 billion and total shareholders&#8217; equity of $398.5 million.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Our Business</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We strive to provide clients with a high level of personalized service while offering a full range of commercial and personal banking products and services. We focus on developing banking relationships that are tailored to meet the individual needs of each client. Our services combine the convenience of modern banking with traditional community bank values. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We focus on serving small- and medium-sized businesses, service professionals and individuals in Santa Cruz County and adjacent Monterey, Santa Clara and San Luis Obispo counties. We attempt to differentiate ourselves by having a high-touch, relationship-driven approach to our client relationships. We use, to the fullest extent possible, the flexibility that results from being an independently owned and operated bank. Our approach to client service includes an emphasis on meeting clients&#8217; specialized banking needs through personal contact by our directors, officers and employees. We are dedicated to relationship banking, which includes ongoing client contact by knowledgeable management and staff, as well as client access to our decision makers with requisite financial solutions and access to capital for their success.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We offer a full complement of lending products, including commercial lines of credit and term loans, land and property development financing, commercial real estate term and asset-based loans, agricultural and farmland loans, including loans under the U.S. Department of Agriculture (&#8220;USDA&#8221;) program and small business loans guaranteed by the Small Business Administration (&#8220;SBA&#8221;), including 7(a) and 504 loans.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">1</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We also offer a full complement of deposit products, including demand deposit accounts, regular savings accounts, individual retirement accounts (&#8220;IRAs&#8221;), health savings accounts (&#8220;HSAs&#8221;), money market accounts and certificates of deposit (&#8220;CDs&#8221;), as well as fully insured deposit products offered through a reciprocal network. We provide treasury management services, electronic bill payment, a full range of mobile banking deposit services, including business mobile banking for on-the-go treasury functions, wire transfers, direct deposits, lockbox and automatic transfers, and remote deposit to electronically capture deposits from business locations. We also provide fraud prevention and card controls, enhancing security and convenience for clients. Our services also include other convenience-related services such as banking by appointment, online banking services, access to a national ATM network and banking by mail to better serve our clients.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our clients are able to access bank services and information through our website, including the ability to access their account information so clients can transact banking business and learn about our product and service offerings. We do not open deposit accounts through the Internet.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Based on the similar nature of the banking products and services offered, we have a single operating segment, which also represents our sole reportable segment. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">No client accounts for more than 10% of total deposits or total loans of the Company as of June 30, 2026.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Market Area</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">A key factor in our ability to achieve our strategic goals and create shareholder value is the attractiveness of the geographic market area in which we operate, which is supported by various industries including tourism, hospitality, retail, engineering and construction, agriculture, technology, government, education, healthcare and other professional services. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are the largest community bank headquartered in California&#8217;s Central Coast region. Our headquarters is located in the heart of downtown Santa Cruz with additional branch offices in Aptos, Capitola, San Jose (relocated from Cupertino effective July 1, 2026), King City, Monterey, Salinas, San Luis Obispo, Scotts Valley and Watsonville, California. Our market area encompasses Santa Cruz County and adjacent Monterey, Santa Clara and San Luis Obispo counties. Our employees are experienced working with businesses and professional service providers in our market area, shown below. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><img alt="branchlocationscroppedwitha.jpg" src="branchlocationscroppedwitha.jpg" style="height:355px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:364px"></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">2</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are a business-focused community bank, with an emphasis on small and medium-sized businesses and professionals, across a wide variety of industries.  We do not target any specific industries or business segments when developing new client relationships, but instead look to the quality of the loan or deposit relationship. The primary driver for business is that we are relationship-oriented with a focus on commercial real estate and commercial and industrial lending. While we have a preference for owner-occupied lending because such loans are typically originated in connection with operating businesses and full relationship opportunities&#59; we, as a relationship-oriented bank, also originate non-owner-occupied commercial real estate loans to meet the broader financing needs of existing long-standing and prospective commercial clients within our market areas. A part of our strategy consists of offering and holding a mix of owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied CRE loans, both of which are generally sourced through relationship channels and also provide opportunities for the Bank to offer a broader range of products and services to a variety of clients, increasing the diversity of our client base. In addition, we believe our merger with 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp enhanced our strategic focus on CRE and commercial and industrial relationship-driven lending, allowing for gains in scale by bringing together two relationship-oriented banking organizations with similar business profiles and similar focus on building long-standing commercial real estate and commercial and industrial lending relationships within our existing market areas where we believe we have significant experience and expertise. While the total amount of our commercial real estate loans (both owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied) increased as a result of the merger, non-owner-occupied CRE loans declined as a percentage of total CRE loans, reflecting slight diversification into owner-occupied industrial loans, medical and general care facility loans  within the overall CRE portfolio post-merger. We believe the lending relationships acquired through the merger are of similar profile to the long-standing core lending relationships that we seek to develop and maintain. Further, while commercial real estate loans, including non-owner-occupied commercial real estate, represent a concentration for us, we believe our comprehensive risk management framework is appropriate to manage our commercial real estate exposures. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are also an SBA Preferred Lender under the SBA Preferred Lender Program, which authorizes us to approve SBA&#8209;guaranteed loans without prior SBA review. As a result, our process for qualifying SBA borrowers and approving SBA loans is more efficient than corresponding processes for lenders that are not SBA Preferred Lenders, which we believe provides us a competitive advantage compared to many of our local competitors. We believe that these factors have contributed to a relatively stable deposit base and consistent demand for loans among the small- and medium-sized businesses, service professionals and individuals in the geographic market area that we serve.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of June 30, 2025, the most recent period for which figures are available as reported by the FDIC, there were 55 financial institutions with 447 offices open in our primary market area of Santa Cruz County and adjacent Monterey, Santa Clara and San Luis Obispo counties. Our total deposits in the market area as of June 30, 2025, were $2.26 billion. from 2024.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Competition</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The banking business in California generally, and in markets we serve, is highly competitive with respect to both loans and deposits and is dominated by a number of regional and national financial institutions that operate offices in our market area and elsewhere. We compete for deposits and loans principally with these financial institutions, as well as community banks, finance companies, non-bank lenders, including &#8220;fintech&#8221; companies, credit unions and other financial institutions operating offices in our market area and elsewhere. Competition among financial institutions is based on interest rates offered on deposit accounts, interest rates charged on loans, other credit and service products, charges relating to products and services, the quality and scope of the services rendered, and, in the case of loans to commercial borrowers, relative lending limits and timely decisions and responses to client needs. The larger financial institutions we compete with have greater resources that may provide them a competitive advantage by enabling them to, among other things, finance extensive advertising campaigns and to allocate their investment assets to regions of highest yield and demand. Many of the competing major commercial banks operating in our service areas offer certain services (such as trust and international banking services) that are not offered directly by us, and, by virtue of their greater total capitalization, such banks have substantially higher lending limits.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The increasingly competitive environment is the result of changes in regulation, changes in technology and product delivery systems, additional non-bank financial service providers and the accelerating pace of consolidation among financial services providers. Banks, securities firms and insurance companies can merge under the umbrella of a financial holding company, which can offer most types of financial services, including banking, securities underwriting and insurance. Also, technology has lowered barriers to entry and made it possible for non-banks to offer products and services traditionally provided by banks, such as automatic transfer and automatic payment systems.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Some of our non-banking competitors, such as fintech lenders, have fewer regulatory constraints and may have lower cost structures. In addition, some of our competitors have assets, capital and lending limits greater than ours, have greater access to capital markets and offer a broader range of products and services than we do.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">4</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our competitive advantage includes the experience and local knowledge of our team members, who understand the communities we serve. Generally, our bankers, officers and directors are actively involved in these communities, which helps us stay connected to the needs of the communities&#8217; individuals and businesses. We believe this community-focused approach strengthens our ability to build lasting relationships. Being locally managed allows us to respond quickly and personally, which differentiates us from larger institutions that often prioritize standardized products and high-volume operations. Our goal is to provide personalized banking services that reflect the values and priorities of the communities we serve.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Our Strategy and Strengths</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We seek to be an innovative, growth-oriented financial institution focused on creating shareholder value through delivering consistent financial performance, developing franchise value, expanding and strengthening client relationships, practicing sound risk management and effectively and prudently managing capital and liquidity.  We also regularly evaluate our product set and market positioning, and&#8212;guided by client feedback, risk analytics and strategic reviews&#8212;selectively expand product and service offerings to strengthen revenue diversity and deepen full&#8209;relationship banking with businesses and individuals across the Central Coast. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We believe the following strengths have been instrumental to the success of our core operations and position us to continue profitable growth and long&#8209;term value creation for shareholders while maintaining a fundamentally sound risk profile.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Community Banking Philosophy.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> We provide a high-touch, relationship-driven, locally focused approach to community banking that pairs direct access to experienced decision&#8209;makers with tailored loan and deposit solutions for businesses and individuals across the Central Coast. Our goal is to provide personalized banking services that reflect the values and priorities of the communities we serve. We deliver local decision&#8209;making and individualized service with a suite of product offerings that we believe are competitive with larger institutions by combining market&#8209;specific expertise in commercial real estate (&#8220;CRE&#8221;), commercial &#38; industrial (&#8220;C&#38;I&#8221;), SBA, and agriculture and treasury services with technology that meets clients&#8217; needs. Generally, our bankers, officers and directors live and work in the communities we serve, which allows for a high level of involvement in local organizations and a deep understanding of the banking needs within our market area. We believe this client&#8209;centric approach underpins long&#8209;term relationship growth and contributes to the quality and stability of our community banking operations. Following our acquisition of 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp on October 1, 2024, we have expanded our footprint and client reach while preserving the high&#8209;touch, relationship-driven community banking model that we believe differentiates us.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Disciplined Credit Culture.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Our relationship managers target borrowers with demonstrated capacity and seasoned operating histories, emphasizing structure, cash&#8209;flow coverage, collateral discipline and concentration management. Individual discretionary limits are complemented by management and board-level oversight to ensure appropriate terms and timely decisions. Consistent with our prudent and disciplined approach to lending and credit risk management, we employ independent loan reviews, rigorous portfolio monitoring, including continuous evaluations of CRE segments, and stress testing where appropriate.  This approach is reflected in our low levels of nonperforming assets and other asset-quality measures relative to our peers, and is supported by a conservative framework in determining the allowance for credit losses.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Conservative Balance Sheet and Capital Position.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> The Bank exceeds the regulatory thresholds to be considered &#8220;well capitalized,&#8221; supporting prudent organic growth and strategic initiatives.  Please refer to section titled &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations - Capital Requirements</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221; under &#8220;Item 2. Financial Information&#8221; of this Registration Statement, for more information concerning our levels of capital and regulatory capital thresholds.  We believe we have ample liquidity to meet our obligations and to fund anticipated loan demand, augmented by our diversified core deposit base and access to market funding. Commercial real estate loans are largely collateralized by multifamily, hotel, retail, office and various other owner and non-owner-occupied properties within our market area. We monitor these loans regularly assessing the borrower&#8217;s cash flow and ability to service debt, supported by internal risk grading criteria. We generally require conservative loan-to-value ratios and personal or corporate guarantees consistent with regulatory guidelines. Adverse economic developments, fluctuations in the real estate market, or an overbuilt market may impact commercial real estate projects and could result in material decreases in the market value of the underlying properties securing such loans, which may result in troubled loans. Further, significant increases in interest rates, changes in market rents, and trends in vacancy rates of commercial properties can impact the credit quality of these loans. Short-term business loans are generally intended to finance short-term working capital and may have payment terms consisting of either interest only or a combination of both principal and interest. Term loans normally provide for floating interest rates with monthly payments of both principal and interest. Generally, our C&#38;I loans are underwritten based on the borrower&#8217;s ability to service such debt from identified cash flows. We monitor these loans through periodic reviews of borrower and guarantor(s) financial performance, including cash flow analysis and debt service coverage, to ensure ongoing repayment capacity. Further, we typically secure a first lien position against the borrower&#8217;s business assets as well as guarantees. Collateral may include real estate, accounts receivable, inventory, equipment or other business assets. While the Company seeks to extend credit to established borrowers, their business cash flows may not materialize as expected, which could place strain on the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay the loan, especially in periods of economic stress. Collateral such as accounts receivable, inventory, equipment and other business assets, can fluctuate in value and may be more difficult to realize their value in periods of economic strain. Further, business cash flows associated with these loans, and economic trends which are influenced by unemployment rates and other key economic indicators, are closely correlated to the credit quality of these loans and a borrower&#8217;s ability to repay their loan. We typically secure first liens on underlying collateral in addition to guarantees. Further, we monitor these loans through regular site inspections prior to approval of periodic draws on these loans. Construction loans are typically structured with an interest-only period during the build phase and mature upon completion of construction with disbursements made as work progresses. Risk with land and construction loans arises from the uncertainty of the borrowers to complete projects within specified cost and timelines, general contractor credit exposure and the builders&#8217; ultimate ability to sell the completed construction. These risks can be exacerbated by changes in the interest rate environment, regulations, supply chain disruptions or labor shortages, any of which may delay completion or reduce the value of the finished property. In addition, local, state or national economic conditions can adversely impact the potential success of construction projects, and the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay the loan.
