Substantially all of our business activities are conducted through the Bank. The Bank operates 10 branches across the California Central Coast and primarily serves small- to medium-sized businesses, which we generally define as businesses with annual revenues of $100 million or less, service professionals and individuals. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We offer a full complement of lending products, including commercial lines of credit and term loans, land and property development financing, commercial real estate term and asset-based loans, agricultural and farmland loans, including loans under the USDA program and small business loans guaranteed by the SBA, including 7(a) and 504 loans.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We also offer a full complement of deposit products, including demand deposit accounts, regular savings accounts, IRAs, HSAs, money market accounts and CDs, as well as fully insured deposit products offered through a reciprocal network. We provide treasury management services including online banking, electronic bill payment, a full range of mobile banking deposit services, including business mobile banking for on-the-go treasury functions, wire transfers, direct deposits, lockbox and automatic transfers, and remote deposit to electronically capture deposits from business locations. We also provide fraud prevention and card controls, enhancing security and convenience for clients. Our services also include other convenience-related services such as banking by appointment, online banking services, access to a national ATM network and banking by mail to better serve our customers.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On October 1, 2024, Bancorp acquired 100% of the outstanding common shares of 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp, the parent company for 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bank, for an aggregate transaction value of $80.8 million.  As of October 1, 2024, 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Capital Bancorp merged with and into Bancorp and 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Capital Bank merged with and into the Bank. Under the terms of the acquisition, the holders of 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp common stock received 0.36 shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock for each share of 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp, resulting in the issuance of 2,071,483 shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock.  With the acquisition, the Company has expanded its geographic footprint and client base.  The Company&#8217;s results of operations include the operating results of 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp, beginning on October 1, 2024.  We may refer to the acquisition of 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp herein as &#8220;the Merger.&#8221;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of June 30, 2026, the Company had total consolidated assets of $2.9 billion, total loans held for investment of $2.3 billion, total deposits of $2.5 billion and total shareholders&#8217; equity of $398.5 million.  As of June 30, 2026, we had 209 full-time equivalent employees. </font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_37"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Critical Accounting Estimates</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We have established and described various accounting policies that govern the application of GAAP in the preparation of the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements. These policies are described in </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Note 1 &#8211; Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> to our audited consolidated financial statements included in &#8220;Item 15. Financial Statements and Exhibits&#8221;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">of this Registration Statement. Certain policies require management to apply estimates and </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">44</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">assumptions made in accordance with GAAP and involving a significant level of estimation and uncertainty, and are reasonably likely to have a material effect on the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities or on the Company&#8217;s results of operations&#59; management considers these to be critical accounting policies. The estimates and assumptions are based on information available at the time, including historical experience and other factors deemed reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results may differ from those estimates, and changes in assumptions could materially affect the Company&#8217;s financial position or operating results in future periods.</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_40"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Allowance for Credit Losses (&#8220;ACL&#8221;)</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We account for credit losses on loans and off-balance sheet loan commitments in accordance with ASC 326, Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses, which requires the Company to record an estimate of expected lifetime credit losses for loans and unfunded loan commitments at the time of origination or acquisition. The ACL is maintained at a level deemed appropriate by management to provide for expected credit losses in the portfolio as of the date of the consolidated statements of financial condition. Estimating expected credit losses requires management to use relevant forward-looking information, including the use of reasonable and supportable forecasts.  The estimation process for determining the ACL requires significant judgment, which involves complex methodologies and various estimates and assumptions. Changes in estimates and assumptions, including those related to economic conditions, could result in material adjustments to the ACL and provision for credit losses in future periods.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The measurement of the ACL for loans is performed by collectively evaluating loans with similar risk characteristics, as well as the individual evaluation of loans that do not share risk characteristics similar to others  in the loan portfolio.  The ACL is measured through the use of a discounted cash flow model that incorporates estimates and assumptions for probability of default and loss given default, which are impacted by forecasts of macroeconomic conditions, such as changes in gross domestic product (&#8220;GDP&#8221;) and the level of unemployment.  We forecast future economic indicators and the resulting expected credit losses over a period of four quarters, which we believe is  reasonable and supportable, followed by reversion to historical averages on a straight-line basis over a period of four quarters.  Estimates of future cash flows are discounted at the loan&#8217;s effective interest rate, adjusted for estimates of prepayments. The ACL for unfunded commitments is determined by applying similar loss factors to those used for funded loans and also incorporates assumptions for the likelihood of funding based on historical utilization of each type of credit commitment.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The use of reasonable and supportable forecasts in the ACL methodology requires significant judgment, such as the selection of forecast periods and the associated economic variables to use when estimating expected future credit losses.  We leverage economic projections from the Federal Reserve&#8217;s FOMC as our reasonable and supportable forecasts used in our ACL model. Although no one economic variable fully correlates to the probability of default, we have identified certain economic variables that have demonstrated strong correlation to actual historical credit losses via regression analysis.  Those economic variables consist of changes in GDP and the unemployment rate.  Further, changes in the interest rate environment can have a significant impact on prepayment speeds, which can influence prepayment assumptions used in the ACL model and ultimately the level of the ACL.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">To demonstrate the sensitivity of our modeled credit losses to key economic parameters, management evaluates how changes in the macroeconomic inputs (GDP growth and unemployment) affect the historical loss rate component of the quantitative ACL estimate. A sensitivity analysis is performed in which a 100-basis point decrease in GDP growth and a 100-basis point increase in the unemployment rate is applied to the economic forecast period of four quarters, followed by reversion to historical averages over a period of four quarters.  This analysis is designed to confirm that the model responds as expected (directionally) to changes in the underlying probability of default loss drivers and to identify the likely magnitude of the changes in selected macroeconomic inputs on the modeled loss expectations for the Bank&#8217;s current portfolio composition. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The sensitivity analysis results in an incremental quantitative impact to the ACL of approximately $1.6 million at December 31, 2025. This result is hypothetical and may not reflect actual increase in lifetime credit losses because (i) the economic environment is highly uncertain, (ii) macroeconomic interrelationships are difficult to predict, (iii) prepayment&#47;curtailment rates of our loans may change as a result of different macroeconomic environment, (iv) adverse conditions can drive credit migration in the loan portfolio, and (v) the sensitivity analysis excludes qualitative adjustments within our ACL framework.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">45</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The ACL methodology also includes adjustments for qualitative factors where appropriate. Please refer to </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Note 1 &#8211; Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> to our audited consolidated financial statements in &#8220;Item 15. Financial Statements and Exhibits&#8221;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">of this Registration Statement for discussion concerning qualitative adjustments.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Although management uses the best information available to derive estimates necessary to measure an appropriate level of the ACL, future adjustments to the ACL may be necessary due to economic, operating, regulatory, and other conditions that extend beyond the Company&#8217;s control. In addition, various regulatory agencies, as an integral part of their examination process, periodically review the Company&#8217;s ACL. Such agencies may require the Company to recognize changes to the ACL based on judgments different from those of management. Further, as the size, complexity, and composition of the loan portfolio changes over time, such as through the acquisition of other financial institutions, new product offerings, client demand for various types of credit, and changes in our geographic footprint, the Company may seek to make additional enhancements to its ACL methodology. Such enhancements may have an impact on the level of the ACL in future periods.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Acquisition Accounting </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company accounts for acquisitions under the acquisition method of accounting in accordance with ASC 805 - </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Business Combinations</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. Purchased assets, including identifiable intangible assets, and assumed liabilities are recorded at their respective acquisition-date fair values. If the fair value of net assets purchased exceeds the consideration given, a bargain purchase gain is recognized. If the consideration given exceeds the fair value of the net assets received, goodwill is recognized. Acquisition related costs, such as severance, data processing expenses and contract termination fees, are expensed as incurred.</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_46"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Recent Accounting Developments</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Accounting Standards Adopted in 2026</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In November 2025, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) 2025-08, </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic 326) - Purchased Loans</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">.  The amendments in this Update expand the population of acquired financial assets subject to the gross-up approach in Topic 326.  Under the provisions of this Update acquired, seasoned, non-purchased credit deteriorated (&#8220;non-PCD&#8221;) assets, such as purchased loans, are accounted for using the gross-up approach at the time of acquisition.  Under this approach, an entity initially recognizes credit losses, in accordance with Topic 326, through an adjustment to the purchase price of the asset.  This approach may be applied to purchased assets that are deemed to be &#8220;seasoned.&#8221;  Acquired non-PCD assets are deemed seasoned if they have been purchased 90 days or more following their origination and where the acquirer was not involved in their origination.  The provisions of this Update provide for all non-PCD loans, excluding credit card receivables, that were acquired in a business combination, to be deemed seasoned under the provisions of this Update.  The amendments in this Update are effective for all entities for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2026 and interim reporting periods within those annual periods.  The amendments in this Update should be applied prospectively to purchased financial assets that are acquired on or after the initial application date. Early adoption is permitted in an interim or annual reporting period in which financial statements have not yet been issued or made available for issuance.  The Company early adopted this Update on January 1, 2026. The adoption of this Update did not have an impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Accounting Standards Issued but Not Yet Adopted</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In September 2025, the FASB issued ASU No. 2025-06, </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Intangibles - Goodwill and Other - Internal-Use Software (Subtopic 350-40),</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> which provides targeted improvements to the accounting for internal-use software. The amendments in this Update modernize and improve the accounting for internal-use software under ASC 350-40 by removing references to prescriptive and sequential software development stages (also referred to as &#8220;project stages&#8221;) and introduces a &#34;probable-to-complete&#34; recognition threshold. Under this Update, entities may begin capitalizing costs once management has authorized and committed to funding the software project and it is probable the software will be completed and used as intended. This Update also consolidates guidance on website development costs into ASC 350-40. The amendments in this Update are effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2027, including interim periods within those annual reporting periods. Early adoption is permitted.  The Company is currently evaluating the provisions of this Update and their impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">46</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In November 2024, the FASB issued ASU No. 2024-03, </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income - Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40), </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">which requires public companies to disclose additional information about certain expenses in the notes to the financial statements. The amendments in this Update are intended to enhance the transparency and usefulness of financial information by requiring entities to break down significant expense categories in the notes to the financial statements in order to address the need for more detailed disclosures about expense categories.  The FASB subsequently issued ASU 2025-01 in January 2025, which clarified the effective date of ASU 2024-03. The amendments in ASU 2024-03 are effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2026, and interim periods within annual periods beginning after December 15, 2027&#59; early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the provisions of this Update, but does not expect adoption to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_49"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Key Factors That May Affect Financial Performance</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We face a variety of risks that may impact various aspects of our financial performance from time to time. The extent of such impacts may vary depending on factors such as the current business and economic conditions, political and regulatory environment, monetary policy, and operational challenges. Many of these risks and our risk management strategies are described in more detail elsewhere in this Registration Statement.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Interest Rates</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Net interest income is the most significant contributor to our net income and is the difference between the interest and fees earned on interest-earning assets and the interest expense incurred in connection with interest-bearing liabilities. Net interest income is primarily a function of the average balances and yields of these interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. These factors are influenced by internal considerations such as product mix and risk appetite as well as external influences such as economic conditions, competition for loans and deposits, and market interest rates.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The cost of our deposits and short-term borrowings is primarily based on short-term interest rates, which are largely driven by the Federal Reserve&#8217;s actions and market competition. The yields generated by our loans and securities are typically affected by both short-term (often impacted by the Federal Reserve&#8217;s actions) and long-term interest rates, which can be driven by market expectation of future inflation, and other market dynamics . The level of net interest income is influenced by movements in such interest rates and the pace at which such movements occur.</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_52"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Results of Operations</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP Financial Measures</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Some of the financial measures discussed herein are non-GAAP financial measures. Generally, a non-GAAP financial measure is a numerical measure of a company&#8217;s financial performance, financial position, or cash flows that exclude (or include) amounts that are included in (or excluded from) the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Taxable equivalent net interest income is derived by adding the tax-equivalent benefit from tax-exempt interest-earning loans and tax-exempt investment securities to total interest income and then subtracting total interest expense. The tax-equivalent benefit is derived using the federal statutory income tax rate of 21%. Taxable equivalent net interest margin is derived by dividing taxable equivalent net interest income by total interest-earning assets for the relevant period. Management considers the use of these measures to be beneficial as they allow for comparability of yields on taxable and tax-exempt assets. We believe disclosure of these measures is also consistent with standard practice within the banking industry. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Return on average tangible equity is derived by adding to GAAP net income the amortization of core deposit intangibles (less the related tax effect), and then dividing the resulting amount by average tangible equity for the period. Average tangible equity is determined by subtracting from average total shareholders&#8217; equity the average balance of intangible assets during the period, which were core deposit intangible assets and goodwill. We believe </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">47</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">that disclosure of return on average tangible equity is beneficial as it provides an understanding of the operating results of our core business. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">These are non&#8209;GAAP financial measures that we believe provide helpful additional information for management and investors, beyond what is shown in our GAAP financial statements. However, non&#8209;GAAP measures have limitations. They should not be considered a substitute for GAAP results and may not be comparable to similar measures used by other banking companies. Other banks may use the same or similar names for non&#8209;GAAP measures but calculate them differently. As a result, caution should be used when comparing our non&#8209;GAAP measures with those of other companies.</font></div><div 2025</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_2224"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Net Income</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Net income for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 was $12.2 million and $27.1 million, respectively, compared to net income of $12.9 million and $24.6 million, for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively, reflecting a decrease of $757 thousand, or 5.9%, for the three months ended June 30, 2026, when compared to the same period ended in 2025, and a $2.6 million, or 10.4%, increase for six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the same period ended in 2025. Diluted earnings per share for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, were $1.16 and $2.59, respectively, compared to $1.22 and $2.31 for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">During the three months ended June 30, 2026, Bancorp early redeemed the remaining higher-cost subordinated debentures that were assumed in the merger with 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp in 2024, resulting in approximately $1.8 million of accelerated purchase discount accretion in the second quarter of 2026. The accelerated purchase discount accretion was recorded within interest expense.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Net income and diluted earnings per share for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to the same period ended in 2025, were impacted by higher interest expense associated with accelerated accretion from the subordinated debt redemption referred to above in the second quarter of 2026, as well as an increase in the provision for credit losses on loans, largely due to year-over-year loan growth. The increase in net income and diluted earnings per share for the six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the same period ended in 2025, was largely due to higher net interest income associated with growth in interest-earning assets and higher noninterest income during 2026.</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_2230"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Net Interest Income</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Net interest income totaled $33.1 million and $67.2 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, reflecting increases of $331 thousand, or 1.0%, and $2.1 million, or 3.2%, for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, when compared to $32.8 million and $65.2 million in net interest income recorded for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis totaled $33.3 million and $67.5 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, reflecting increases of $358 thousand, or 1.1%, and $2.1 million, or 3.2%, when compared to $32.9 million and $65.4 million in tax-equivalent net interest income recorded for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively. See the section titled </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP Financial Measures</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> for a reconciliation of net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis, a non-GAAP financial measure, to net interest income, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The increase in net interest income for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the same periods ended in 2025, was primarily the result of higher interest income on loans stemming from year-over-year growth in average loan balances, as well as an increase in interest income associated with higher average balances of interest-earning cash and investment securities. The year-over-year increase in interest income for both the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the same periods ended in 2025, was partially offset by higher interest expense, largely attributed to the subordinated debt redemption and higher interest expense on deposits due to strong deposit growth over the last year. These increases in interest expense were partially offset by the absence of interest expense on FHLB advances during the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the same periods in 2025, as strong year-over-year deposit growth has allowed the Bank to rely less on wholesale funding to support the growth in interest-earning assets. For the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, total interest income was $42.9 million and $84.7 million, respectively, reflecting increases of $2.1 million, or 5.1%, and $4.1 million, or 5.1%, for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, when compared to $40.8 million and $80.6 million in total interest income recorded for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively. Total interest expense was $9.8 million and $17.5 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, reflecting increases of $1.8 million, or 22.0%, and $2.0 million, or 13.2%, for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, when compared to $8.0 million and $15.5 million in total interest expense recorded for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively. </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">51</font></div></div></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_2273"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Net Interest Margin</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The net interest margin was 4.90% and 4.99% for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to 5.28% and 5.27% for the same periods in 2025. The taxable equivalent net interest margin, a non-GAAP financial measure, was 4.92% and 5.01% for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to 5.30% and 5.30% reported for the same periods in 2025. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The year-over-year decrease in the net interest margin and taxable equivalent net interest margin was largely due to the subordinated debt redemption, which negatively impacted the net interest margin by approximately 27 basis points and 14 basis points during the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively. In addition, a year-over-year decrease in the taxable equivalent yield on interest-earning assets for both the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, also contributed slightly to the decrease in the net interest margin and taxable equivalent net interest margin in 2026. This was largely associated with a year-over-year change in the overall mix of and yields on interest-earning assets, including a lower overall yield on loans due in part to certain loan products indexed to the prime rate that re-priced lower because of a 75-basis-point reduction in the Federal Funds target rate in late 2025. In addition, the yield on loans was impacted by a year-over-year decrease in purchase discount accretion on loans acquired from 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp of approximately $803 thousand and $1.7 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Net interest margin is derived by dividing net interest income by total average earning assets for the period. Taxable equivalent net interest margin, as presented in the tables below, is calculated by dividing taxable equivalent net interest income by total average earning assets for the period.  Fluctuations in market interest rates, as well as changes in the volume and composition of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, may materially affect both net interest income and net interest margin. Management actively monitors these measures and seeks to optimize net interest income while maintaining an acceptable level of interest rate risk through established asset and liability management policies.  Interest rate risk is managed by evaluating the pricing, maturity, and repricing characteristics of all classes of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">See the section titled </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP Financial Measures</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> for a reconciliation of t</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">axable-equivalent net interest margin,</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> a non-GAAP financial measure, to net interest margin, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The following tables set forth the major components of taxable-equivalent net interest income, which is a non-GAAP measure, and the related yields and rates for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025. Interest income from investment securities and loans has been presented on a taxable-equivalent basis. GAAP interest income and the associated GAAP yield for these components is also provided in footnote (2) of the table below. style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The provision for credit losses is based on management&#8217;s assessment of the adequacy of our allowance for credit losses. Factors impacting the provision include inherent risk characteristics in our loan portfolio, the level of nonperforming loans and net charge-offs, both current and historic, economic and credit conditions, the direction of the change in collateral values, and the funding probability on unfunded lending commitments. The provision for credit losses is recorded as a charge against current period earnings in order to maintain our allowance for credit losses, which reflects management&#8217;s best estimate of current expected credit losses in our loan portfolio at the balance sheet date.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The provision for credit losses for both funded and unfunded commitments was $1.5 million and $1.2 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $620 thousand and $2.0 million for the three and six months ended June 2025, respectively. The provision for credit losses for loans was $1.4 million and $1.3 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $420 thousand and $1.9 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively. The increase in the provision for credit losses for loans for the three months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the same period in 2025, can be attributed in large part to the growth in loans during the second quarter of 2026, as well as an increase in specific reserves on individually evaluated loans, primarily due to declines in collateral value. The decrease in provision for credit losses for loans for the six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the same period in 2025 is largely due to higher growth in construction loans during the first half of 2025, which carry a higher estimated reserve factor than other loans in the portfolio.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Bank recorded a provision for credit losses for unfunded commitments of $128 thousand for the three months ended June 30, 2026, and a reversal of provision for credit losses on unfunded commitments of $103 </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">55</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">thousand for the six months ended June 30, 2026. for the three months ended June 30, 2026, was $15.9 million, compared to $15.4 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025, representing an increase of $420 thousand, or 2.7%. The increase can be attributed to higher salaries and employee benefits, higher occupancy and furniture and equipment costs and an increase in other expenses. The $357 thousand increase in salaries and employee benefits is attributed to higher employee salaries and commissions expense as well as higher stock-based compensation costs including annual director stock grants. These increases were partially offset by year-over-year decreases in group insurance costs and higher salary deferrals associated with increased loan originations in 2026. The combined $437 thousand increase in occupancy and furniture and equipment costs can be attributed in part to our expansion into the San Jose market. The $230 thousand increase in other expenses was due in part to $129 thousand in costs associated with a land development property the Bank foreclosed upon in the first quarter of 2026, as well as higher other miscellaneous expenses. Partially offsetting these increases in noninterest expense was a $207 thousand reduction in marketing and business development expenses, a $217 thousand decrease in data and item processing costs and the absence of $97 thousand in acquisition-related expenses incurred in 2025 in connection with the acquisition of 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp. </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">57</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The decrease in marketing and business development costs was largely due to the absence of rebranding-related expenses that were incurred during 2025, while the decrease in data and item processing costs resulted from one-time credits received from our core system processing vendor during 2026.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Total noninterest expense for the six months ended June 30, 2026, was $31.9 million, compared to $30.9 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025, representing an increase of $959 thousand, or 3.1%. The increase can be attributed to higher professional fees, salaries and employee benefits, furniture and equipment costs and other expenses, partially offset by decreases in marketing and business development expenses, lower data and item processing costs and the absence of acquisition-related expenses in 2026. The increase in professional fees is due to costs associated with our ongoing preparation to become an SEC registrant. The increase in salaries and employee benefits is attributed to higher employee salaries, commissions expense and stock-based compensation costs. These increases were partially offset by higher salary deferrals associated with a year-over-year increase in loan originations. The increase in furniture and equipment expenses can be attributed in part to our expansion into the San Jose market. The increase in other expenses can be attributed to higher miscellaneous expenses as well as $134 thousand in expenses incurred during the first six months of 2026 associated with a property the Bank foreclosed upon in the first quarter. Partially offsetting these increases in noninterest expense were lower marketing and business development costs and data and item processing costs that were previously discussed.</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_2267"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Income Tax Expense </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Provision for income taxes for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 was $4.8 million and $10.9 million, respectively, compared to $5.2 million and $10.0 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively. The effective tax rate was 28.18% and 28.65% for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to 28.78% and 28.92% for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively. The decrease in the effective tax rate for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the same periods in 2025 can be attributed to overall slightly higher favorable permanent tax differences in 2026, due in part to an increase in tax-exempt interest income when compared to 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The effective tax rate differs from the federal statutory rate primarily due to the impact of state taxes as well as the mix and amount of various permanent tax differences, including tax-exempt income from municipal securities, loans and bank-owned life insurance policies, tax benefits associated with low-income housing tax credit investments, and stock-based compensation, among others. </font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_70"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Results of Operations for Years Ended December 31, 2025 and 2024</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_73"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Net Income</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Net income for the year ended December 31, 2025, was $50.4 million, or $4.76 per diluted share, compared to $29.6 million, or $3.28 per diluted share earned during the year ended December 31, 2024. The increase of $20.9 million, or 70.5%, was largely driven by the Merger with 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp that closed on October 1, 2024, reflecting a full year of merged operations, as well as a reduction in one-time Merger-related expenses.  </font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_85"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Interest Income</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Total interest income was $167.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $119.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, an increase of $47.5 million, or 39.7%. The increase in interest income was primarily driven by an increase in average interest-earning assets stemming from the Merger, which added approximately $603.1 million in loans and approximately $258.3 million in investment securities at the time of the Merger. Interest income for 2025 also benefited from a full year of discount accretion on loans acquired in the Merger, totaling approximately $9.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $3.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. In addition, organic loan growth throughout 2025, and, to a lesser extent, an increase in the yield on the investment portfolio and higher balances of interest-earning cash also contributed to the increase in interest income during 2025.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">58</font></div></div></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_91"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Interest Expense</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Total interest expense was $32.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $24.5 million for the previous year ended December 31, 2024, an increase of $8.4 million, or 34.3%. The increase in interest expense was driven by an increase in the balance of interest-bearing liabilities, stemming from the Merger, as well organic deposit growth, partially offset by an overall decrease in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities.  The year-over-year decrease in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities was due, in part, to slightly lower average rates on money market deposits and time deposits, as well as the absence of higher cost brokered deposits in 2025. These benefits to the cost of funds in 2025 were partially offset by $1.0 million in accelerated accretion on the early partial redemption of $5.3 million of subordinated debentures assumed in the Merger. </font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_79"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Net Interest Income</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Net interest income totaled $134.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $95.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. The increase in noninterest income is partially attributed to increased volume of fee generating transactions as a result of the inclusion of a full year of operations of 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp in 2025 after the close of the Merger on October 1, 2024. As a result of the Merger, the Company also acquired additional bank-owned life insurance as well as additional stock in the Federal Home Loan Bank of San Francisco, both contributing to respective increases in earnings on bank-owned life insurance and dividends on non-marketable equity securities during 2025. In addition, noninterest income during 2024 included $507 thousand in losses on the sale of other assets, due primarily to the sale of a branch building resulting from post-Merger consolidation. $50.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, an increase of $12.0 million, or 23.9%. The increase in noninterest expense during 2025 was primarily the result of an expansion of our branch footprint due to the Merger and the associated impact on various components of noninterest expense. Salaries and employee benefits, which increased $9.3 million, or 37.7%, from 2024 to 2025 was the result of the expansion of our workforce due personnel retained from the Merger. The number of full-time-equivalent employees was 223 as of December 31, 2025, as compared to 152 as of September 30, 2024, prior to the Merger. In addition, amortization of core deposit intangible assets increased $2.9 million during 2025 which can be attributed to amortization of the additional core deposit intangible assets recognized as part of the Merger. We also incurred higher professional fees during 2025 which is associated with the preparation of becoming an SEC registrant. Further, the increase in marketing, business development and shareholder related expenses can be attributed to $502 thousand of costs incurred in 2025 associated with our rebranding project and changing the Bank&#8217;s name to West Coast Community Bank. These increases in noninterest expense were partially offset by a $6.4 million decrease in one-time acquisition-related expenses in 2025. The majority of one-time acquisition related expenses were incurred in the fourth quarter of 2024 and are attributed to the Merger with 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp.</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_115"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Income Tax Expense </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Provision for income taxes was $19.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $12.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, an increase of $7.3 million from the year ended December 31, 2024. The effective tax rate was 28.02% and 29.47% for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. A $28.1 million increase in income before income taxes, stemming from the Merger, partially offset by a slight decrease in the effective tax rate for 2025, led to the increase in the provision for income taxes when compared to 2024.  The decrease in effective tax rate in 2025 from 2024 was primarily due to the absence of non-deductible acquisition-related expenses incurred in 2024, benefits from investments made in low-income housing tax credit (&#8220;LIHTC&#8221;) partnerships in 2025, higher average balances of tax-exempt municipal investments which were acquired through the Merger, as well as adjustments to prior year income taxes after filing of the 2024 income tax returns in 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The effective tax rate for each year differs from the federal statutory rate primarily due to the impact of state taxes as well as the mix and amount of various permanent tax differences, including tax-exempt income from municipal securities, loans and bank-owned life insurance policies, tax benefits associated with LIHTC investments, and stock-based compensation, among others. For a full reconciliation of our effective tax rates from the statutory tax rate for both years, refer to </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Note 13 - Income Taxes</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> to the audited consolidated financial statements included in &#8220;Item 15. The decrease in net income for 2024 was attributed, in part, to $7.1 million in acquisition-related expenses and $7.7 million in Day 1 provision for credit losses on acquired non-PCD loans, both associated with the Merger with 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp in the fourth quarter of 2024. </font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_130"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Interest Income</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Total interest income was $119.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, compared to $94.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2023, an increase of $25.2 million, or 26.7%. The increase in interest income during 2024 was primarily due to increase in average interest-earning assets stemming from the Merger, as previously discussed, as well as higher yields on loans and investment securities. Loan yields benefited from new loan pricing, higher market interest rates, as well as $3.8 million in purchase discount accretion associated with loans acquired from 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp. While the average balance of investments was lower during the year ended December 31, 2024, compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, the impact of increased yields more than offset the impact that a decline in average balances had on interest income. Higher yields on the investment portfolio was the result of maturities and paydowns on lower-yielding securities, as well as higher yielding additions to the portfolio including </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">64</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">securities acquired in the Merger. The increase was due to higher volume and the shift in the mix of interest-bearing liabilities throughout 2024, including higher balances of money market, time deposit and brokered deposits.  This, in conjunction with continued upward pressure on deposit pricing, contributed to the increase in interest expense during 2024.  Further, average interest-bearing liabilities increased during 2024 due to the Merger, which, as of the acquisition date, added approximately $501.4 million in interest-bearing deposits and $11.5 million in subordinated debt.  This contributed to the increase in interest expense during 2024.</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_127"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Net Interest Income</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Net interest income totaled $95.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, compared to $82.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2023.  Net interest income on a taxable equivalent basis totaled $95.4 million for the year December 31, 2024, compared to $82.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2023, an increase of $13.0 million, or 15.7%. </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">See the section titled </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP Financial Measures</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> for a reconciliation of </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis, </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">a non-GAAP financial measure, to net interest income, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The increase in net interest income during the year ended December 31, 2024, was largely the result of an increase in average interest-earning assets, reflecting higher average loan balances during the year, primarily attributable to loans acquired in the Merger, totaling approximately $603.1 million at the time of the Merger. Net interest income for 2024 also benefited from purchase discount accretion associated with loans acquired in the Merger totaling $3.8 million during 2024. For the year ended December 31, 2024, the taxable equivalent yield on the investment securities portfolio was 2.32% compared to 1.52% for the year ended December 31, 2023. The increase was due to reinvestment of portfolio cash flows at higher market yields in addition to one calendar quarter of income on the higher yielding securities portfolio acquired in the merger with 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp. The taxable equivalent yield for the year ended December 31, 2024, for the loan portfolio was 7.18% compared to 6.66% for the year ended December 31, 2023. The increase was also due to higher yields on new loan production.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The increase in net interest income in 2024 was partially offset by a $12.4 million increase in interest expense as compared to 2023, primarily due to an increase in average balance of interest-bearing liabilities assumed from the Merger and the rates associated with those interest-bearing liabilities.  The rate paid on interest-bearing liabilities increased to 2.40% during the year ended December 31, 2024, from 1.38% during the year ended December 31, 2023. The increase was the result of continued market pressures on deposit pricing in response to market competition, particularly money market accounts, and due to a 100 basis point increase in the federal funds rate during 2023.</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_136"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Provision for Credit Losses</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The provision for credit losses, for both funded and unfunded commitments, was $7.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, compared to a provision for credit losses of $1.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2023. We invest in a variety of investment securities consistent with regulatory guidelines and internal risk management objectives, primarily to provide liquidity, taking into consideration the loan pipeline, deposit trends and other contingencies. These securities may be pledged to secure state and local agency deposits, borrowings or liquidated to generate cash proceeds. In addition, the investment portfolio plays an important role in managing interest rate risk, given that the maturity structure and rate characteristics of these assets can be adjusted in response to changes in loan and deposit composition. After meeting liquidity and interest rate risk management needs, we seek to optimize earnings balanced with credit risk exposure. Securities within the investment portfolio are classified as either AFS or HTM at the time of purchase, in accordance with applicable accounting standards.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The portfolio mix, shown in detail in the tables below, is diversified and includes securities issued by the U.S. government and its agencies, state and local municipalities, as well as smaller allocations to securities from private issuers. During the six months ended June 30, 2026, the balance of the investment portfolio decreased $3.0 million, driven by maturities, calls, principal repayments, and sales totaling $49.6 million and a decrease in the fair values of the AFS portfolio resulting from an increase in intermediate-term interest rates (5-10 years), partially offset by purchases of agency and agency mortgage-backed securities totaling $47.5 million. During the year ended December 31, 2025, the balance of the investment portfolio decreased $16.6 million, driven by maturities, calls, principal repayments, and sales totaling $138.3 million, partially offset by purchases of agency and agency mortgage-backed securities totaling $106.4 million and an improvement in the fair values of the AFS portfolio resulting from a notable decline in intermediate-term-interest rates (5-10 years).</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of June 30, 2026, we had $6.4 million in investment securities classified as HTM and $381.7 million in investment securities classified as AFS, compared to $6.5 million classified as HTM and $384.6 million classified as AFS, as of December 31, 2025. Net unrealized losses on AFS securities totaled $9.0 million at June 30, 2026, compared to $6.4 million at December 31, 2025. The increase in net unrealized losses on AFS securities can be attributed to increases in interest rates during 2026.  As of December 31, 2024, we had $7.3 million of investments classified as HTM and $400.5 million as AFS. Net unrealized losses on AFS securities totaled $18.8 million at December 31, 2024. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our investment securities portfolio consists of U.S. Treasury securities, U.S. government-guaranteed mortgage-backed securities (&#8220;MBS&#8221;) and collateralized mortgage obligations (&#8220;CMO&#8221;), obligations of state and political subdivisions, Small Business Administration (&#34;SBA&#34;) backed securities, obligations of U.S. government-sponsored </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">68</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">agencies, private label CMO, asset-backed securities and corporate bonds.
