Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Total loans held for investment were $2.3 billion at June 30, 2026, compared to $2.2 billion at December 31, 2025, representing an increase of $98.9 million, or 4.6%. The increase was primarily due to organic growth of lending in both legacy and newer markets, such as San Luis Obispo County. Outstanding loans made to new relationships established in 2026 totaled $141.5 million at June 30, 2026, with an average loan size of $2.7 million.  Total loans held for investment increased $127.2 million during 2025 when compared to the $2.0 billion reported at December 31, 2024. The increase was primarily due to organic growth of lending in both legacy and newer markets, principally in Silicon Valley. Outstanding loans made to new relationships established in 2025 totaled $117.0 million at December 31, 2025, with an average loan size of $1.2 million. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Commercial and industrial loans were $397.4 million at June 30, 2026, compared to $369.8 million at December 31, 2025, representing an increase of $27.5 million, or 7.4%. The increase in commercial and industrial loans can be attributed to organic growth concentrated in revolving lines of credit. Commercial and industrial loans comprised 17.5% and 17.0% of the total portfolio at June 30, 2026, and December 31, 2025, respectively. Commercial and industrial loans increased $70.7 million during 2025 when compared to the $299.1 million reported at December 31, 2024. The increase during 2025 can be attributed to organic growth concentrated in revolving lines of credit. Commercial and industrial loans comprised 14.6% of the total portfolio at December 31, 2024. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We have exposures to loans secured by CRE due to the nature of our market and the credit needs of our clients. Management and the Board manage and monitor the Bank&#8217;s CRE exposures through a comprehensive risk management framework that includes regular review of CRE concentration metrics, CRE portfolio trends, third-party credit reviews and borrower-level stress testing results, established risk-based lending standards and review of internally established concentration limits. CRE concentrations and related stress-testing results are reviewed quarterly by the Directors&#8217; Loan Committee and Board of Directors as part of the Bank&#8217;s risk management process. The Bank has adopted policies which require management to proactively monitor concentration exposures and to evaluate recommendations to the Directors&#8217; Loan Committee and Board for risk-limiting actions, including restrictive credit terms and&#47;or participations, whenever concentrations approach or exceed 90% of approved guideline limits or when stress-testing results reflect heightened downside risk within a concentration category. Further, we typically originate CRE loans to clients within our primary market areas in which we have substantial expertise, and believe that our long-term experience in CRE lending, underwriting policies, as well as our loan and credit monitoring and administration procedures, are generally appropriate to managing our CRE concentrations.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our non-owner-occupied CRE loans have credit characteristics that differ from our owner-occupied CRE loans because repayment generally depends more directly on the income-producing capacity of the underlying property, including rental income and occupancy, rather than on the operating cash flows of a business occupying the property. As a result, the performance of these loans is more closely tied to property-level operating results, market conditions and the ability to refinance the loan.</font></div><div of approximately $67.0 million, or 5.0%, from $1.3 billion at December 31, 2025, and comprised 61.5% and 61.3% of the total portfolio at June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively. The increase in CRE loans was driven by an expansion in loan originations in the San Luis Obispo region, specifically in agricultural and retail real estate loan types. Commercial real estate loans at December 31, 2025 were largely unchanged when compared to $1.3 billion at December 31, 2024, and comprised 65.2% of the total portfolio at December 31, 2024. The commercial real estate portfolio has the highest concentration in hotel, multifamily, and industrial properties.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">CRE loans increased $521.8 million, or 64.3% in 2024, driven predominantly by loans acquired in the merger with 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp, which closed on October 1, 2024. The increase in owner-occupied CRE loans was $168.1 million from December 31, 2023, to December 31, 2024, more than 85% of which was attributable to the loans acquired from 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp with the rest due to organic growth. Almost the entire increase in non-owner-occupied CRE loans in 2024 was attributable to the acquisition from 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp. Although non-owner-occupied CRE in 2024 increased in absolute dollars, non-owner-occupied CRE loans declined as a percentage of total CRE loans to 73.0% at December 31, 2024 from 76.6% at December 31, 2023, reflecting a higher concentration in non-owner-occupied CRE loans prior to the merger with 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp, and a diversification to owner-occupied industrial loans, medical and general care facility loans within the overall CRE portfolio during 2024.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Land and construction loans at June 30, 2026, were $261.8 million compared to $253.1 million at December 31, 2025, representing an increase of $8.7 million, or 3.4%. The increase in land and construction loans was driven by construction focused lenders in the Silicon Valley region. Land and construction loans comprised 11.5% and 11.7% of the total portfolio at June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively.  Land and construction loans increased by $62.1 million, or 32.5%, during 2025 when compared to the $191.0 million reported at December 31, 2024. The increase in land and construction loans was driven by the onboarding of construction focused lenders in the Silicon Valley region. Land and construction loans comprised 11.7% of the total portfolio at December 31, 2025, compared to 9.3% of the total portfolio at December 31, 2024.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">SBA, B&#38;I, FSA loans at June 30, 2026, were $170.5 million compared to $181.5 million at December 31, 2025, representing a decrease of $11.0 million, or 6.1%. and Six Months Ended June 30, 2026 and 2025</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Gross charge-offs on loans were $953 thousand and $4.6 million, for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $7 thousand and $12 thousand for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025. Charge-offs for the second quarter of 2026 were mainly due to a $912 thousand charge-off on a loan acquired from the merger with 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp. In addition to the charge-off just discussed, charge-offs for the first six months of 2026 were also due to a $3.1 million charge-off recorded in the first quarter of 2026 of a previously established specific reserve associated with a land development loan that was transferred to other real estate owned status at the time of charge-off. Gross recoveries totaled $9 thousand and $312 thousand for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $36 thousand and $39 thousand for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The allowance for credit losses as a percentage of loans held for investment was 1.55% at June 30, 2026, compared to 1.76%, as of December 31, 2025. The decrease in the allowance for credit loss as a percentage of loans held for investment from December 31, 2025 was mainly due to the previously discussed $3.1 million charge-off of specific reserves during the first quarter of 2026, as well as overall changes in the mix of the collectively evaluated portfolio during 2026.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">For the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, the Bank recorded a provision for credit losses on the funded portfolio of $1.4 million and $1.3 million, respectively. The provision for credit losses on the funded portfolio was $420 thousand and $1.9 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025. The increase in the provision for credit losses for the three months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the same period in 2025, can be attributed in </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">76</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">large part to the growth in loans during the second quarter of 2026, as well as an increase in specific reserves on individually evaluated loans, primarily due to declines in collateral value. The decrease in provision for credit losses for the six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the same period in 2025 is largely due to higher growth in construction loans during the second quarter of 2025, which carry a higher estimated reserve factor than other loans in the portfolio, as well as unfavorable changes in the economic forecasts used in the ACL model as of June 30, 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Our Board of Directors is ultimately responsible for ensuring policies and procedures are in place that provide for prudent management of assets and liabilities of the Bank and to ensure these policies are effectively implemented. Management establishes liquidity guidelines and reviews our ongoing compliance with the policies approved by the Board of Directors. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The objective of liquidity management is to manage cash flow and liquidity reserves so that they are adequate to fund our operations and to meet obligations and other commitments on a timely basis and at a reasonable cost. We have developed tools to appropriately identify, measure, monitor, and control funding and liquidity risk. These tools include daily, monthly, and quarterly liquidity status reports and risk measures, cash flow projections, stress testing, and a formalized Contingency Funding Plan (&#8220;CFP&#8221;) for measuring and managing liquidity risk.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our primary sources of funds are the deposit inflows, periodic and maturity payments of principal and interest on loans, investment securities sales, maturities and paydowns, federal funds purchases, FHLB and FRB advances, other borrowings, and cash flow from operations.  Our primary uses of funds are withdrawals of deposits (including maturities of certificates of deposit), loan originations, the purchase of investment securities, repayment of borrowings, dividends to common shareholders, share repurchases and operating expenses. As of June 30, 2026, management believes the above-mentioned sources will provide adequate liquidity during the next twelve months for the Bank to meet its operating needs.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We seek to maintain an appropriate level of liquid assets and formal lines of credit with the FHLB, FRB and correspondent banks to ensure a safe and sound operation. Our liquid assets are comprised of unrestricted cash, short-term investments, and unpledged AFS investments securities. Our liquidity position is enhanced by our ability to raise additional funds as needed in the wholesale markets.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of June 30, 2026, total on&#8209;balance&#8209;sheet liquidity was $383.0 million, and total external contingent liquidity capacity was $1.2 billion, resulting in total available liquidity sources of $1.6 billion.  As of December 31, 2025, total on&#8209;balance&#8209;sheet liquidity was $457.9 million, and total external contingent liquidity capacity was $1.2 billion, resulting in total available liquidity sources of $1.6 billion. The decrease in on-balance-sheet liquidity during the first six months of 2026 can be attributed in part to loan growth during 2026, with the deployment of excess cash into new loan originations.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">84</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Bancorp is a corporation separate and apart from the Bank and, therefore, must provide for its own liquidity, including liquidity required to pay dividends to its shareholders. Bancorp&#8217;s main source of cash flow is dividends declared and paid to it by the Bank and its ability to issue debt and raise capital. There are statutory and regulatory limitations that affect the ability of the Bank to pay dividends to Bancorp without regulatory approval. See the section titled &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Business&#8212;Supervision and Regulation</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221; for more information.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">A use of liquidity for the Company is shareholder dividends. Bancorp paid dividends to its shareholders totaling $4.9 million during the six months ended June 30, 2026, and $8.7 million and $6.2 million during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. We expect to continue our current practice of paying quarterly cash dividends with respect to our common stock, subject to the Board of Director&#8217;s discretion to modify or terminate this practice at any time and for any reason without prior notice. We believe our quarterly dividend rate per share, as approved by our Board of Directors, enables us to balance our multiple objectives of managing our business and returning a portion of our earnings to our shareholders. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Capital Requirements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Bancorp and the Bank are subject to various regulatory capital adequacy requirements administered by banking regulatory agencies. These requirements involve quantitative measures of assets, liabilities and certain off-balance-sheet items calculated under regulatory accounting practices. Capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by regulators. Failure to meet minimum capital requirements can result in mandatory and discretionary supervisory actions by regulators that could have a direct material effect on the Company&#8217;s financial statements. Management believes that as of June 30, 2026, December 31, 2025, and 2024, both the Bank and Bancorp met all capital adequacy requirements to which they are subject. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As described in </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Supervision and Regulation - The Bank - Capital Requirements,</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> the Bank is subject to prompt corrective action regulations. The prompt corrective action framework provides five capital classifications&#58; &#8220;well capitalized,&#8221; &#8220;adequately capitalized,&#8221; &#8220;undercapitalized,&#8221; &#8220;significantly undercapitalized&#8221; and &#8220;critically undercapitalized.&#8221; For insured depository institutions that are adequately capitalized (and not well capitalized), regulatory approval is required to accept brokered deposits. Insured depository institutions that become undercapitalized are subject to limitations on capital distributions, as well as asset growth and expansion, and must submit capital restoration plans. At June 30, 2026, December 31, 2025, and 2024, the Bank was categorized as well capitalized under this regulatory framework. There are no conditions or events since that notification that management believes have changed the Bank&#8217;s category. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Federal Reserve also sets regulatory capital requirements for bank holding companies. Because Bancorp qualifies under the Federal Reserve&#8217;s Small Bank Holding Company Policy Statement, it is generally not subject to </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">85</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">consolidated regulatory capital ratio requirements. Instead, the Federal Reserve looks through Bancorp to evaluate capital at the Bank&#8217;s level capital ratios. Nevertheless, the following table shows the Bancorp&#8217;s capital ratios as if it were subject to separate capital measurements. Actual and required capital amounts and ratios are presented below for both the Bank and Bancorp as of the dates indicated&#58; </font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><table See </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Note 9 &#8212; Borrowed Funds</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">, </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Note 6 &#8212; Leases</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> and </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Note 17&#8212; Loan Commitments and Other Related Activities</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> to the audited consolidated financial statements, as well as </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Note 8 &#8212; Leases, and Note 9 &#8212; Subordinated Debentures </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">to the interim unaudited consolidated financial statements, both of which are included in &#8220;Item 15. Financial Statements and Exhibits&#8221;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">of this Registration Statement for additional information regarding sources of liquidity and contractual commitments and obligations.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">88</font></div></div></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_229"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_232"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Market Risk</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Market risk represents the potential for loss resulting from adverse changes in the market value or pricing of financial instruments. Our market risk primarily arises from interest rate risk inherent in its lending, investment, deposit-taking, and funding activities. To address this significant component of market risk, management actively monitors and manages interest rate exposure.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our profitability is sensitive to fluctuations in interest rates. A sudden and material change in interest rates across different points on the yield curve may adversely affect earnings if the rates applicable to assets and liabilities do not adjust at the same pace, magnitude, or on comparable terms. We monitor the impact of interest rate changes on net interest income with the primary objective of minimizing adverse effects on net interest income and capital, while structuring its asset-liability mix to optimize the yield-cost spread. The Asset&#47;Liability Committee (&#8220;ALCO&#8221;) of the Board of Directors meets at least quarterly to review interest rate risk and related strategies.</font></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_235"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Interest Rate Sensitivity</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Interest rate risk represents the potential impact on earnings and asset values from changes in market interest rates. This risk arises primarily from timing differences in the repricing of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, embedded options such as loan prepayments, and shifts in the yield curve.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We manage interest rate risk through ALCO. Strategies include adjusting the mix and repricing characteristics of the loan and investment portfolios, entering into interest rate hedging contracts, as well as managing the rate and maturity structure of deposit products offered and wholesale funding sources utilized.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Management employs tools such as net interest margin projection reports, and interest rate simulations under various scenarios to monitor exposure and ensure compliance with ALCO limits. The simulation model is based on the maturity and repricing characteristics of our interest rate sensitive assets and liabilities. The model also incorporates various assumptions, which management believes to be reasonable but may have a significant impact on the results. What can deviate from the modeled scenarios include the timing and magnitude of changes in interest rates, the yield curve evolution and shape, the correlation between various interest rate indices, financial instruments&#8217; spread relative to benchmark rates. The modeled results are highly sensitive to deposit mix and deposit beta assumptions, which are derived from a regression analysis of our historical deposit data.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">While actual outcomes cannot be predicted with certainty, these models help assess potential impacts on net interest income and capital. If potential changes to the net equity value and net interest income resulting from hypothetical interest rate changes are not within the limits established by ALCO, we may adjust the asset and liability mix to bring the risk position within the limits or take other remediation actions.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The following table presents the estimated effect of instantaneous parallel shifts of interest rate yield curve on our projected net interest income over the next 12 months, assuming no balance sheet growth, as of the dates indicated. The scenarios presented are hypothetical and are not indicative of expected interest rate movements.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><table Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">89</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of June 30, 2026, model simulations indicate that projected net interest income over the next 12 months is less sensitive to declining interest rate scenarios than it was as of December 31, 2025. This change was primarily driven by a reduction in rate-sensitive cash and cash equivalents as a percentage of earning assets at June 30, 2026 compared to December 31, 2025 and an increase in commercial real estate loans. While yields on cash and cash equivalents adjust immediately with changes in market interest rates, our commercial real estate loans generally have an initial five-year fixed-rate period. In addition, interest-bearing deposits comprised a larger share of total deposits as of June 30, 2026, compared to December 31, 2025, increasing the extent to which deposit costs decline when interest rates fall.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Conversely, our model simulations as of December 31, 2025 indicate that our projected net interest income over the next 12 months is more sensitive to falling interest rate scenarios in comparison to our simulation results as of December 31, 2024, reflecting a year&#8209;over&#8209;year increase in downside sensitivity, primarily due to an increase in our cash and cash equivalents in 2025. A larger proportion of assets in cash and cash equivalents would result in repricing immediately when interest rates fall and reduce our projected interest income. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our model simulation results show an asymmetrical change in net interest income in rising interest rate scenarios compared to falling interest rate scenarios for all periods presented. This asymmetry is primarily driven by higher assumed deposit betas on interest-bearing deposits in rising rate environments. In rising market rate scenarios, we modeled greater pass-through of market rate increases to our interest-bearing deposit accounts, hence reducing the projected interest income benefit. Conversely, in declining interest rate scenarios, we modeled lower deposit repricing betas, as management believes that it would be more difficult to pass through market rate decreases to interest-bearing deposit accounts, especially for those accounts bearing below-market interest rates. These assumptions reflect management&#8217;s judgment based on historical experience, competitive conditions, and current market dynamics and may differ from actual deposit repricing behavior.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">90</font></div></div></div><div id="ie5d8a2464b1940dba7e2d852c1fb6667_244"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Item 3. Properties</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our headquarters are located at 75 River Street, Santa Cruz, California, where we lease 14,395 square feet of space, with such lease expiring in 2033. As of June 30, 2026, the Bank operates full-service branch offices in Aptos, Capitola, Cupertino, King City, Monterey, Salinas, Scotts Valley, San Luis Obispo, Santa Cruz, and Watsonville. The Bank has also entered into an agreement to lease a facility in San Jose and on July 1, 2026, the Cupertino branch was relocated to this location. In addition, the Bank entered into an agreement to lease an office in San Mateo in August 2026 and expects to occupy the facility in September 2026. As of June 30, 2026, the Bank owns the branch buildings in Salinas and Monterey and leases its remaining facilities, with leases expiring in various periods between 2026 and 2033. A majority of the leases provide for the payment of taxes, insurance, maintenance, and certain other operating costs associated with the leased premises in addition to the monthly rental payments. Many of the leases contain escalation clauses and extension provisions that have various renewal options of three to five years each.  </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We believe all of our existing facilities are adequate for our present and anticipated future use. For additional information regarding properties of the Company and information regarding leases, please see </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Note 5 &#8212; Premises and Equipment</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> and </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Note 6 &#8212; Leases</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> of the audited consolidated financial statements, as well as </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Note 8 &#8212; Leases</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> of the interim unaudited consolidated financial statements, both of which are included in &#8220;Item 15. All Board committees may address risks directly with management or, where appropriate, may elevate a risk for consideration by the full Board. As a result, all Board members become familiar with a wide range of matters affecting the Company and are able to oversee risk by exposure to, and interaction with, the Company, its people and its processes. Board members are encouraged to attend all committee meetings as circumstances permit. While the Board does not involve itself in the day-to-day operations of our business in accordance with corporate governance principles, the Board oversees our business and monitors the performance of management, including with respect to risk management. Management is responsible for the day-to-day management of risk and implementation of appropriate risk management controls and procedures, including by assessing and managing the risks the Company faces, including strategic, operational, regulatory, investment and execution risks, on a day-to-day basis, and reporting to the Board regarding the Company&#8217;s risk management processes, including quarterly enterprise risk management assessments and annual cyber, BSA&#47;anti-money laundering and third-party risk assessments. The Company&#8217;s senior management is also responsible for creating and recommending to the Board for approval appropriate risk appetite metrics reflecting the aggregate levels and types of risk, including credit, market, liquidity, interest rate and compliance, the Company is willing to accept in connection with the operation of its business and pursuit of its business objectives. Management carries out its responsibilities with respect to this topic through the Enterprise Risk Management Committee, which is comprised of the Company&#8217;s executive officers and other members of senior management.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Audit Committee is primarily responsible for monitoring and oversight of the accounting and financial reporting process of the Company, the audits of our financial statements and the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting. The Audit Committee also assists the Board in discharging its oversight duties with respect </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">99</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">to risk assessment and risk management, and the adoption and implementation of associated policies and practices. The Audit Committee is also focused on assisting the Board in monitoring and overseeing internal audit function, and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements. In accordance with its charter, the Audit Committee is responsible for ensuring that the Company has in place an appropriate enterprise-wide process to identify, prioritize, measure, monitor and report alignment of our practices with its defined risk appetite, including for example, operational, fraud, third-party relationships involving critical activities and&#47;or risks, technology, information security, anti-money laundering, compliance, model, legal, reputational, and strategic risks. The Compensation Committee has primary responsibility for risks and exposures associated with the Company&#8217;s compensation policies, plans and practices, regarding both executive compensation and the Company&#8217;s compensation structure generally. In particular, the Compensation Committee, in conjunction with members of the Company&#8217;s management team, reviews the Company&#8217;s incentive compensation arrangements to ensure these programs are consistent with applicable laws and regulations, including safety and soundness requirements, and do not encourage imprudent or excessive risk-taking by our employees. The Governance and Nominating Committee oversees risks associated with the independence of the Board, potential conflicts of interest, succession planning and governance related risks. The Loan Committee is also focused on assisting the Board in its monitoring and oversight of credit processes and asset quality as well as compliance with applicable regulatory requirements. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Code of Ethics </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Board has adopted a &#8220;code of ethics&#8221; that requires Bancorp&#8217;s directors, officers (including the principal executive officer, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer or controller and persons performing similar functions) and employees to conduct business in accordance with the highest ethical standards and in compliance with all laws, rules and regulations applicable to us. Box 8426, Santa Cruz, California 95061-9958, Attention&#58; Maxwell Sinclair, Corporate Secretary, and following the listing of our common stock on Nasdaq, on the Company&#8217;s website at www.wccb.com.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Insider Trading Policy</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We also maintain an Insider Trading Policy that governs the purchase, sale, and&#47;or other disposition of the Bancorp&#8217;s securities by our directors, officers, employees, certain consultants and the immediate family members of each of the foregoing, that we believe is reasonably designed to promote compliance with insider trading laws, rules, and regulations and the listing standards of Nasdaq. Our Insider Trading Policy generally prohibits executive officers, directors, and employees from purchasing any financial instruments (such as prepaid variable forward contracts, equity swaps, collars, or exchange funds), making short sales of Bancorp&#8217;s securities, or otherwise engaging in any transactions that hedge or offset any decrease in the market value of Bancorp&#8217;s securities or limit the ability to profit from an increase in the market value of Bancorp&#8217;s securities. During 2025, the Governance and Nominating Committee held three regular meetings and no special meetings.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">No member of our Compensation Committee is, or formerly was, an officer of ours. Executive Compensation</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Overview</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The primary objective of our executive compensation program is to attract and retain highly skilled and motivated executive officers that significantly contribute to the Company&#8217;s success. The executive officers are expected to manage the Company to promote its growth and profitability, minimize risk, and advance the interests of our shareholders. As such, the Company&#8217;s compensation program is designed to provide levels of compensation that reflect the executive&#8217;s role in the organization and reward the individual&#8217;s performance within the context of the Company&#8217;s performance.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our compensation policies are designed to attract and retain highly qualified personnel. Such compensation may include elements that reward long-term financial performance and growth of Bancorp in the form of restricted stock and grants of stock under our 2014 Omnibus Plan, 2024 Equity Based Compensation Plan, and retirement benefits under our 401(k) Plan, in addition to short-term elements such as salary and bonus opportunity. The goal of restricted stock awards and other forms of equity compensation, which serve as long-term incentive compensation, is to attempt to more closely align the interests of the award recipient with the long-term interests of shareholders. Our general strategy, including the compensation paid to executive officers, is to pay annual compensation that is competitive with similar positions at peer group banks, with consideration given to our overall financial condition and performance relative to banks in similar positions. Compensation for executive officers may also include participation in the Bank&#8217;s Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan to provide competitive retirement benefits and termination severance benefits under executive employment agreements with the goal of retention of executive officers and continuity of management over the long-term development of the Company. In determining compensation benefits, including compensation of executive officers, the Compensation Committee obtains salary information and surveys from industry trade associations and may consult with independent compensation and benefits experts. The granting of restricted stock awards and other forms of equity incentive compensation is based on an officer&#8217;s responsibilities and relative position in the Bank and is recommended by the Compensation Committee to the Board for approval.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Compensation Committee also continually reviews the Company&#8217;s compensation policies to identify any practice that might encourage an employee to expose the Company to unacceptable risk. At the present time, the Committee is satisfied that the current executive compensation program does not encourage the Company&#8217;s executive officers, including the named executive officers (&#8220;NEOs&#8221;), to expose the Company to inappropriate risk. The Compensation Committee is composed of independent directors who review and assess general compensation and benefits policies for Bancorp in accordance with its charter.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As an emerging growth company under the JOBS Act, we have opted to comply with the executive compensation disclosure rules applicable to &#8220;smaller reporting companies&#8221;, as such term is defined in the rules promulgated under the Securities Act, and with which emerging growth companies may comply, which permit us to limit reporting of executive compensation to our principal executive officer and our two other most highly compensated executive officers. This section provides an overview of our executive compensation program, including a narrative description of the material factors necessary to understand the information disclosed in the summary compensation table below.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:8.68pt">The stock option awards granted vest 25% on each anniversary of the grant date for four years.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Elements of Compensation</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Base Salary</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Base salary represents the fixed portion of the compensation of our executive officers and is an important element of compensation intended to attract and retain highly talented individuals and motivate top-tier performance. Annual base salaries for executive officers are based on the executive&#8217;s experience, individual performance for the </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">108</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">prior year and our prior year financial results, among other factors considered by the Compensation Committee. We also consider comparative peer salary data and believe that base salaries are set at levels that enable us to hire and retain individuals in the banking and finance industry that can drive achievement of the Company&#8217;s overall objectives.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Compensation Committee reviews executive salaries on an annual basis.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Short-Term and Long-Term Incentive Compensation</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our executive compensation program also includes short-term incentive compensation in the form of a cash bonus and long-term incentive compensation in the form of equity awards, typically restricted stock awards that vest ratably over a three-year period and contingent upon continued service. The cash awards and long-term incentive compensation awards were granted subject to the achievement of corporate financial goals as well as personal goals based on the Compensation Committee&#8217;s evaluation of actual results compared to the established incentive compensation targets per the annual incentive compensation program. For 2025, each NEO had a total incentive compensation target as follows&#58; for Ms. Snelling, 75% of base salary and for Ms. Situ and Mr. De Bernardo, 50% and 33% of base salary, respectively. The total incentive compensation target for each executive was divided between short and long-term incentive compensation as follows&#58; for Ms. Snelling, 67% short-term and 33% long-term&#59; for Ms. Situ and Mr. De Bernardo, 80% short-term and 20% long-term. We believe this mix of short-term and long-term incentive compensation appropriately aligns the incentives of our NEOs with those of our shareholders.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Performance-Based Incentive Compensation</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Compensation Committee may also award discretionary compensation, in the form of performance-based equity compensation, to NEOs. The Compensation Committee may select as performance factors a range of financial and non-financial performance metrics such as achievement of strategic objectives among other items when determining the amount, form and achievement targets for the discretionary compensation, if any, for each NEO.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In 2025, Ms. Snelling, Ms. Situ and Mr. De Bernardo were granted restricted stock to be vested ratably over four years after the grant date, contingent upon achievement of strategic goals of the Company, and applicable service conditions, in the following amounts based on the grant-date fair value of the stock</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">$1.1 million, $400 thousand and $310 thousand</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">, </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">respectively, as shown in the &#8220;Stock Awards&#8221; column of the Summary Compensation Table. These performance-based awards have not been earned or vested during 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Other Compensation &#38; Benefits</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Supplemental Executive Retirement Program (&#8220;SERP&#8221;)</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">During 2005, in an effort to attract and retain qualified officers, the Bank implemented a supplemental executive retirement program for the benefit of certain executive officers of the Bank. Ms. Snelling, Ms. Situ and Mr. DeBernardo participate in the SERP. The SERP consists of two benefit components &#8211; a defined retirement benefit and an endorsement split dollar death benefit. Each of the participating executives is a party to two agreements with the Bank &#8211; a Supplemental Executive Salary Continuation Agreement and a Split Dollar Life Insurance Agreement, that describe the participant&#8217;s respective benefits and any restrictions that apply to those benefits. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Subject to stipulated tenure requirements contained in each SERP agreement, the defined retirement benefit portion of the SERP entitles Ms. Snelling, Ms. Situ, and Mr. DeBernardo to a monthly retirement benefit for 15 years. Normal retirement occurs upon resignation after age 65. Early retirement is an option under stipulated circumstances. If they retire at normal retirement age, the benefits for Ms. Snelling are $7,083.33 per month, and the benefits for Ms. Situ, and Mr. DeBernardo are $6,000 per month. The benefit ceases upon the participant&#8217;s death. An early retirement election subjects the participant to lifetime benefit-amount penalties. For a stipulated number of years of continuous full-time employment with the Bank, the participant accumulates credit toward eligibility for a full benefit, in a manner analogous to vesting. However, such accumulated credit can be forfeited entirely under certain conditions, such as the participant&#8217;s termination of employment with cause, or the participant&#8217;s voluntary resignation before reaching their early retirement age. Upon Disability as defined in the SERP, the participant will </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">109</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">receive a single payment in the amount of the Accrued Benefit (as defined in each SERP agreement) in lieu of any other benefit. In the event Ms. Snelling, Ms. Situ, or Mr. DeBernardo experience a Separation from Service (as defined in each SERP) in connection with a change in control (as defined in the SERP) or within 24 months thereof, the applicable percentage of the retirement benefit that the participant is entitled to receive upon normal retirement will accelerate to 100%.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Participants are also provided a death benefit. This benefit is an endorsement split dollar life insurance benefit, in a defined amount that is the lesser of one million dollars, or eighty percent of the amount by which the death benefits of the respective BOLI policies exceed their cash values. The cash value equals the value at which the BOLI policies are carried on the books of the Bank. The Bank is entitled to the remainder of the policy proceeds. The Bank has no obligations to the participants to pay death benefits if the BOLI policies for any reason do not pay death benefits in excess of their respective cash values. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of December 31, 2025, the value of projected benefit obligation was $123 thousand for Ms.&#8239;Snelling, $180 thousand for Mr.&#8239;DeBernardo, and $12 thousand for Ms. Situ. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">401(k) Plan</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our 401(k) Plan is designed to provide retirement benefits to all eligible full-time and part-time employees. All employees are eligible to participate in our 401(k) benefit plan, which is a tax-deferred savings plan designed to assist employees in preparing for their retirement years. The 401(k) Plan allows employees to contribute to the plan up to certain limits prescribed by the Internal Revenue Service. We match 30% of contributions up to 6% of compensation.  </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Health and Welfare Benefits</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our NEOs are eligible to participate in the same benefit plans designed for all of our eligible full-time and part-time employees, including health, dental, vision, disability and basic group life insurance coverage, on the same basis as other participants. The purpose of our employee benefit plans is to help us attract and retain quality employees, including executives, by offering benefit plans similar to those typically offered by our competitors. The Company utilizes a fully funded medical plan and pays a portion of the premium attributable to each employee. The Company utilizes a self-funded dental plan.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Perquisites</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We provide our NEOs with a limited number of perquisites that we believe are reasonable and consistent with our overall compensation program and better enable us to attract and retain superior employees for key positions, as described in the &#8220;All Other Compensation&#8221; column to the Summary Compensation Table above.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Employment Agreements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Employment Agreement with Ms. Snelling</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. Effective January 1, 2026, the Bank entered into an employment agreement with Ms. Snelling pursuant to which she serves as Chairman of the Board of Directors, and as the Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of the Bank and Bancorp. The agreement replaced Ms. Snelling&#8217;s previous employment agreement entered into on January 1, 2025, and as described in greater detail below, increased her base pay and expanded her severance benefits.  </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The agreement includes payment of a base salary per year of $715,000, which is subject to an annual review by the Board and adjustments, if any, as may be approved at the discretion of the Board of Directors. At the end of each calendar year, the amount of bonus compensation, if any, to be paid to Ms. Snelling is to be determined in the sole discretion of the Board of Directors based upon the implementation of the Bank&#8217;s strategic plan and profitability for each year. The agreement provides for other incidental compensation and benefits, including flexible vacation paid, group life, health, accident and disability coverages for Ms. Snelling and her dependents, and reimbursement for business expenses. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The agreement is an at-will contract that may be terminated by either party at any time. Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Company Transactions with Related Parties</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our board of directors adopted a written policy designed to promote compliance with all applicable requirements concerning related party transactions, including those of the SEC and Nasdaq. Transactions that are determined to be related party transactions in accordance with our policy are referred to the board of directors for approval. In determining whether to approve a related party transaction, the board of directors considers, among other factors, the fairness of the proposed transaction, the direct or indirect nature of the related party&#8217;s interest in the transaction, the appearance of an improper conflict of interests for any director or executive officer taking into account the size of the transaction and the financial position of the related party, whether the transaction would impair an outside director&#8217;s independence, the consistency of the transaction with regulatory expectations, and the potential violations of other corporate policies.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The following is a description of each transaction since January 1, 2023 in which&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">We have been or are to be a participant&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">the amount involved exceeds or will exceed $120,000&#59; and </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">any of our directors, executive officers, or beneficial holders of more than 5% of our common stock, or any immediate family member of or person sharing the household with any of these individuals (other than tenants or employees), had or will have a direct or indirect material interest and is not otherwise subject to an exemption from disclosure.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Bank, during the normal course of business, has made loans and provided other banking services to the directors and executive officers of the Company, including their family members and businesses and professional organizations with which they are associated, and management expects that the Company and the Bank will continue to engage in such banking transactions in the future. Such loans and other banking services were made in the ordinary course of business, were made on substantially the same terms, including interest rates and collateral, as those prevailing at the time for comparable loans and banking services with persons not related to the Company or the Bank, and did not involve more than the normal risk of collectability or present other features unfavorable to the Company or the Bank. Neither the Company nor the Bank has engaged in any transaction reportable pursuant to Item 404 of Regulation S-K during the periods specified herein.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of June 30, 2026, $17.3 million of total loan commitments were extended to individuals who, during 2025, were executive officers, directors or affiliates of the Company&#59; of these total commitments, approximately $8.0 million were outstanding loan balances as of June 30, 2026. Recent Sales of Unregistered Securities</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The following information represents securities sold by the Company within the past three years through the date of this Registration Statement which were not registered under the Securities Act. Included are new issues, securities issued in exchange for property, services or other securities and new securities resulting from the modification of outstanding securities.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Share-Based Compensation</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company maintains equity-based compensation plans for employees and non-employee directors to promote alignment with shareholder interests and support long-term performance objectives.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">2003 Qualified Stock Option Plan</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Bank adopted a qualified stock option plan (the &#8220;Option Plan&#8221;) for employees, non-employee directors and Bank founders, under which a maximum of 1,000,404 shares of common stock was available be issued. The Option Plan calls for the exercise prices of the options to be equal to or greater than the fair market value of the stock at the time of grant. Options granted to Bank founders who are not also directors or Bank officers were fully vested upon the date of grant. All other options granted provide for daily vesting over the first four years of the option contract. All director and employee option contracts have expiration dates on the earlier of termination of service or 10 years from the date of grant. The Option Plan expired during 2014 and was replaced with the 2014 Omnibus Plan (the &#8220;2014 Plan&#8221;).  </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">All options granted under the Option Plan have a 10-year term and have been issued with exercise prices at the fair market value of the underlying shares at the date of grant. The non-qualified stock option awards to the organizers vested 100% immediately, whereas regular stock option awards to directors and employees vest over a four-year period from the date the options were granted. The remaining 320 options were exercised in 2023 resulting in the plan having no shares remaining for issuance.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">2014 Omnibus Equity Compensation Plan</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Bank adopted the 2014 Plan in May 2014, which remained in effect until February 19, 2024. The 2014 Plan permitted the grant of incentive stock options to employees and non-qualified stock options and restricted stock awards to officers and non-employee directors. The maximum number of shares of common stock authorized under the 2014 Plan was 939,940, of which 444,399 shares remained available for issuance when the plan expired in February 2024. The 2014 Plan has been replaced by the 2024 Plan and no additional awards can be granted from this plan.  At June 30, 2026, options to purchase shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock totaling 193,795 at a weighted ,average price of $22.95 per share remain outstanding under the 2014 Plan. At June 30, 2026, there were a total of 8,658 unvested restricted stock awards outstanding under the 2014 Plan. A copy of the 2014 Plan is included as an exhibit to this Registration Statement, see Exhibit 10.1.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">2024 Equity-Based Compensation Plan</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company adopted the 2024 Plan in May 2024, which will remain in effect until March 20, 2034. The plan authorizes the grant of incentive stock options to employees and non-qualified stock options, restricted stock awards, restricted share units, and performance share awards to officers and non-employee directors. The maximum number of shares of common stock that may be issued under the 2024 Plan is 1,000,000, of which 826,975 shares were available for future grants as of June 30, 2026.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Awards under the 2024 Plan are administered by the Compensation Committee of the Board, which determines the terms and conditions of each award, including vesting requirements and exercise prices, subject to the provisions of the Plan. A copy of the 2024 Plan is included as an exhibit to this Registration Statement, see Exhibit 10.2.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Set forth below is information for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, concerning the issuance of shares under equity compensation plans.
